analysis.body:
# US Grid Interconnection Snapshot: September 2026

Across the five major US grid operators, 8,365 generator and storage projects totaling 1.33 million MW are in interconnection queues as of early September 2026. This represents generation and storage capacity waiting to connect—not data center demand itself—but the composition of what's queuing tracks load patterns. Storage alone accounts for 328,106 MW of these requests, concentrated in ERCOT (159,820 MW), MISO (68,429 MW), and Southwest Power Pool (52,913 MW), while gas capacity waiting to connect stands at 184,509 MW across all operators. ERCOT dominates by scale with 438,086 MW across 1,778 requests, followed by NYISO at 319,095 MW and MISO at 299,721 MW.

Solar and wind make up the largest fuel categories by count. Solar comprises 277,759 MW (21 percent of total capacity) spread across 2,076 requests, while wind accounts for 167,666 MW across 1,459 requests. These renewables dominate ERCOT's queue (150,347 MW solar, 48,183 MW wind) and SPP's queue (33,534 MW solar, 64,737 MW wind). Gas queuing suggests grid operators and developers expect sustained peak demand that renewables alone cannot cover without storage, and the 328,106 MW of storage requests indicates serious effort to address intermittency—though whether this capacity will come online fast enough relative to data center load growth remains unresolved.

Commercial-sector electricity sales across eight major states totaled 54,798 MWh in June 2026, with Texas consuming 15,754 MWh (29 percent of the sample), California 10,025 MWh, and Virginia 7,771 MWh. These sales serve as a proxy for data center load since data centers are billed mostly as commercial customers, though the measure conflates all commercial use. Prices ranged from $8.66 per MWh in Texas to $27.33 in California, making Texas and Virginia the low-cost poles and California the high-cost region—a gap that will likely shape where new data center capacity seeks connection points. Watch whether ERCOT's gas-queue submissions accelerate or flatten as queue projects begin moving from study to construction phases, which will signal whether interconnection timelines are compressing or extending.
